newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosch 96 sales up, profit unsatisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Bosch 96 sales up, profit unsatisfactory.

text.p: German electrical engineering company Robert Bosch GmbH said on Thursday its sales grew 15 percent in 1996 while profits were unsatisfactory, falling just short of the 1995 level.
The company said sales rose to 41.2 billion marks ($25.1 billion) last year including acquisitions but that excluding acquisitions, sales growth was more modest at five percent to 37.6 billion.
Chief executive Hermann Scholl told a news conference late on Wednesday that income from ordinary activities in 1996 almost matched the 1995 level of 1.65 billion marks.
He added that while sales would show further clear growth in 1997 profits would rise only slightly. ($ = 1.640 German Marks)

"The operating profit of the Bosch group was unsatisfactory in 1996, as it was in 1995," Scholl said. "Profit almost matched the 1995 total but given the sales growth this means a worsening in percentage terms."
Scholl said there were two reasons for the negative development. First, domestic customers were no longer prepared to pay a premium for car components or communications technology made in Germany.
That means German manufacturers have had to cut their prices to keep up with cheaper foreign products.
In addition, Bosch had in recent years locked itself into long-term contracts with carmakers which included fixed annual price reductions in a bid to maintain or expand market share, Scholl said.
German labour costs rose at the same time as prices fell, so operating profit came under pressure, Bosch said.
To avoid the gap between costs and prices widening further the company would have to boost its share of foreign production, it said.
Bosch also predicted sales would grow 7.4 percent in 1997. Referring to profits, Scholl said, "We don't expect to make a big jump but we expect small progress."
